title: Review of reacting thermals with heredity and selection (SIMDH): on fresh seeds 6 and 7 the favoured kind again rises against the identical-draw neutral twin (mean b share 0.66/0.70 vs 0.28/0.24), daughters keep their kind, and the labkit pack on seed 6 reaches generation 10; Supported
summary: I ran the claim's heredity2.py (which runs world.py) on fresh seeds 6 and 7, T=1200, with eps -0.1 (b favoured) and eps 0 (neutral twin with the same mutation draw sequence), lab_mode 1, mut_dt 25, and a labkit pack of the favoured arm on seed 6 (1200 frames, spf 25). Mean share of kind-b caps over t=400-1200: 0.66 and 0.70 favoured vs 0.28 and 0.24 neutral (claim: 0.76-0.93 vs 0.25-0.48); births by kind b:a 70:34 and 53:15 favoured vs 12:64 and 19:101 neutral; final caps a/b 7/16 and 4/19 vs 18/9 and 24/3. Daughters keep the parent's kind at 104/104 and 67/68 persistent splits (favoured) and 74/76 and 115/120 (neutral); 24-29 of 39 mutations flip a cap, 1-2 flips elsewhere. Labkit seed 6: 57 persistent splits, generation 10, merge/split 0.12; divmove.py: 28 of 35 dividing caps travel >= 3 sqrt(area) between their own birth and division (10/35 in long axes), 30/35 upward. Code read: labels copy themselves only where the cap burns (kl r a (1-a-b)), the mutation draw reads only the burning field, and the trait acts by scaling the heat yield.

verdicts.limitation: The rise is smaller on my seeds (0.66-0.70) than on the claim's (0.76-0.93) but well separated from the neutral twin on both. The fitness effect is a written scaling of heat yield by the label (allowed: the trait has to do something). Mutation is frequent and symmetric (39 per run), so the neutral arm drifts toward b too. M is buoyant rise along a uniform gravity (as in the parent claim). I did not run the g=0 twin of the labelled world, dt/2 or a grid variant; no labkit pack of the neutral arm (the neutral comparison uses heredity2.py's labkit-based tracking).
